# CHAPTER 5: RESONANCE OF THE LOST

**The tides have shifted. Following a daring and successful mission to the ancient derelict VEILED SHADOW, Team Gamma has returned to the Altisian fleet with life-saving technology and a prize beyond measure: the SEVENTH MOON, a freighter brought back from the dead.**

**But the victory is tempered by a haunting discovery. The Wayfinder recovered on Bespin is no mere map—it is a KEY. And the VEILED SHADOW is its LOCK. Aboard the ship, an ancient Force-ghost has named the young Mandalorian, WES DEL-FIN, as the PATHFINDER, tasked with reawakening a hidden network of Force-conduits that could lead the Jedi to a sanctuary far from the reaches of the rising EMPIRE.**

**Amidst the heavy weight of destiny, a flicker of light remains. MARINA CLOUDSPINNER, Wes’s partner and the mother of his unborn child, has been raised to the rank of JEDI KNIGHT. Now, with the fleet’s survival hanging on a razor’s edge, the team plunges back into the treacherous KARTHON EXPANSE. Their mission: to turn the key, harmonize the ship’s heart, and reclaim a legacy that has waited in the silence for four thousand years....**

The blue-white tunnel of hyperspace outside the *Seventh Moon’s* viewport is a steady, mesmerizing blur. Inside the cockpit, the atmosphere is a study in quiet, professional preparation. The ancient Ghtroc freighter feels significantly more robust than it did during its maiden flight out of the derelict; the reinforced mandible plating and the tuned capacitors provided by Chief Gaxx’s teams have smoothed out the ship's previously erratic vibrations.

Wes sits in the co-pilot's chair, the weight of the Wayfinder case resting just behind him, a silent anchor in the Force. Marina sits behind him in at the operations station, her movements confident and precise as she monitors the core's stability. Behind them, in the main hold, the "Fixer" droids sit in their magnetic cradles, their single eyes dark and unblinking.

Kaelen leans back in the pilot’s, his hands resting lightly on the control yokes, his grey eyes fixed on the time-to-reversion clock. **"She’s handling like a different ship, Wes,"** he grunts, his voice carrying a rare note of genuine satisfaction. **"The forward drift is gone, and the power coupling isn't screaming at me every time I adjust the pitch. Gaxx’s team knows their business."**

He glances at the nav-comp. **"We’re coming up on the end of the primary leg to clear Karthos Prime’s shadow and then the jump through 'Korta’s Passage'. Travel time will be just under four hours. We're right on schedule."**

Leaning back into the copilot's chair Wes let out a slow breath.   Outside the viewport he watched the blue-white hyperspace tunnel.   He wondered what, if anything, would be different when the Wayfinder was used to travel between the known spacelanes.  It was something that they would have to wait to find out.  There was still the job of freeing the *Shadow* from the *Whispers* to tackle first.  


He listened to and felt the two others next to him.   Next to him in the pilot's chair was Kael.   The pilot was calm and measured as always.   The team had come to trust the man’s skill and ability behind the controls of whatever he flew.   


Sitting right behind Wes was Marina.   He could feel the confidence within her.   It felt like the promotion the Council gave her solidified her confidence.  She, like all of them, had been through some rough times.  Doubted herself yet took the chance to leave it all behind to come to the Praxium.   He turned toward the center, the chair rotated with him and he looked at her.   He smiled when she turned and gave him a quick look and smile.  She was quick to back so she could  monitor the readings. 


Kael’s movements had Wes turning back to the front.   The pilot was comfortable.  Wes would even say somewhat at ease considering where they were heading back to.   As Kael spoke about the ship Wes understood the  man's feelings.  Wes nodded as he tapped on his control panel.  **”They put a lot of work into her for us.”**  He shifted gears and followed up on the flight path mentioned.   **”Will we be able to use the same corridor as before?”**

Kael shifts slightly in his seat, his hands making minute adjustments to the sublight trim even while in hyperspace. He taps a series of calculations on his secondary screen before answering. **"The 'Korta's Passage' leg is fixed coordinates, so that stays the same. But the sublight approach through the Graveyard Shallows is a different story. Commander Heston’s data confirmed that the *Shadow* has a slow, unpredictable drift. The debris field out there isn't static either."** 

He glances at Wes, his expression grimly professional. **"I've updated the entry vector based on Korta’s latest projections. We’ll be aiming for the same quadrant, but I’ll have to fly the final kilometers on visual and short-range sensors again. If the drift has shifted the hangar's orientation, we might have a trickier time getting into that maintenance alcove than we did before."**

Wes looked at the plotted course and the projected, possible drift of the  *Shadow.*  Kael was right, it could be tricky.  **”Understood.  Less than four hours.”**  He tapped on his bracer to set a timer for three hours.   **”When we reach the Graveyard Shallows we can reassess the approach vector.   We’ll need eyes on it before we can make any final approach decisions.  Keep us updated.  I’ll check back and let me know if you need a break.”**  Wes gave the seasoned pilot a nod, grabbed his helmet and stood.  **”Also since we’re not boarding a hostile ship this time would you like to join the team?   Your skills could prove useful in any number of places.”**


He looked at Marina who was still looking over the operations station.  **”Shall we go talk plans with the others for the reintegration of the Wayfinder to the *Shadow?*”**

Kael grunts, his eyes never leaving the blue-white tunnel of hyperspace. **"I appreciate the invite, Wes, but I’m a pilot. My place is here… in the chair. If things go sideways, you'll want the engines already hot."**

Marina unplugs her datapad from the operations station and stands, her movements slightly stiff after the period of intense focus. She smooths her robes over the subtle curve of her abdomen.  **"He's right, Wes. Having Kael on the bridge is a security measure in itself."** She offers a warm, tired smile, her presence in the Force steadying. **"Let's go. Sera and the others are likely finished with their initial gear checks by now."**

Wes and Marina descend the short ladder from the cockpit, moving through the ship's compact neck into the main lounge and engineering hub. The *Seventh Moon* feels different today—the oppressive layer of ancient dust is gone, replaced by the faint, sharp scent of cleaning solvents and fresh hydraulic fluid. The lighting here is bright and steady, reflecting off the clean metallic surfaces. 

In the central lounge area, the rest of Team Gamma has claimed the available space. Roric is seated on a cargo crate, methodically running a diagnostic on his ion rifle, the weapon's power cell humming softly. Echo is standing near the primary ramp, her gaze fixed on a small holographic display projecting the *Veiled Shadow’s* interior map. Sera is perched on the edge of the circular lounge seating, her legs swinging as she taps away at her specialized slicing rig, which is currently tethered to one of the ship’s auxiliary data ports.

Wes gave Kael an affirmative nod.  He understood the pilots and Marina’s reasoning.   **”Undersrood and vigilant eyes on the ship and our path of egress, if needed, is a good thing.”**  He gave Kael’s shoulder an affirmative thump.  The same he’d done numerous times with fellow Mandalorians.  Though this time not nearly as hard since the pilot wasn’t wearing armor.   


At Marina’s mention of the others he smile.  **”Lead the wash Cyar’ika.  I want to know what Sera and the others have planned for the return trip.”**  Sera was an expert slicer and now that she had an idea of what to expect on the *Shadow.*  He expected she would be even more prepared this go around.   

Less than a minute later the two of them were entering the central lounge.   There, the  rest of the crew was located in different positions.  All seeing totasks that were important to the mission.  


Sera looked up from her slicing rig as her legs continued to swing back and forth.   The Zeltron, always seeming to be in a good mood, smiled.   Wes smiled back as he walked near Marina.   **”Were four hours from dropping out of hyperspace we here we’ll begin our flight path to the *Shadow.*”**


He looked at the team he was taking back into the massive ship that was somehow part of his past.  Some long forgotten tradition that was one reawakened.  He steadied himself within the Force.  It was something that he knew Marina would sense through their bond.   **”I’m happy you're all here and coming back with us.”**  He said looking at Marina quickly before looking back.  **”I'm guessing this second time around we are a little more prepared.  Updates?”**  He asked looking at Roric and then to Exho and Sera as they each finished.

Roric doesn't look up from his ion rifle immediately, his fingers finishing a delicate adjustment to the cooling shroud before he finally clicks the safety on. **"Double-stocked on power packs for the rifles and we still have a stock of ion grenades,"** he grunts, his voice a low rumble that feels grounding in the vibrant lounge. **"Chief Gaxx threw in a couple of high-output power packs for the 'Fixers' as well. If we hit heavy resistance, we've got enough disruption to keep a battalion of those droids busy."**

Echo taps the holographic map, causing a section of the *Veiled Shadow’s* mid-decks to pulse with a yellow warning light. **"I've refined the route through Maintenance Corridor 7. It's the tightest path, but it offers the most cover from the ship's internal sensor sweeps—assuming they're even active."** She looks at Wes, her sharp eyes reflecting the blue glow of the display. **"I've also marked every structural instability Gaxx flagged. If we have to move the *Moon* or the team in a hurry, we know which bulkheads won't take the pressure."**

Sera finally detaches her rig from the ship’s port, a satisfied smirk playing on her lips. **"And for the main event,"** she chirps, her crimson skin practically glowing under the lounge lights. **"I've successfully slaved the *Seventh Moon’s* long-range transceiver to a dedicated sub-space channel. It's essentially a high-powered signal booster. Once we’re inside the bay, this ship will act as a lighthouse. We should be able to maintain a clear data-link between our suit comms and the *Moon*."**

She leans back, looking around at the gathered team. **"I’ve also been digging into those Pathfinder logs Marina found. If we can get someone to the main computer core on the bridge, I might be able to broadcast a system-wide signal. It might put the entire security grid on our side. It's a gold mine of an asset just sitting up there waiting to be tapped."**

Wes nodded as each Ror, Echo and Sera all gave an update.   They had all clearly been busy and taken to tasks that would help on the return trip to recover the *Shadow.*  From the little fixers, to mapping the *Shadow* and possible ship wide communications, they had the potential to have a complete one-eighty from the first foray which surprisingly only days ago.   


**”Good work.  My thought is that the way in will be like the way out.   Uneventful, due to what the Custodian did before he faded away.”**  He looked at Roric and Echo and gave the two an approving nod.   


He looked at Sera and pointed.  **”Good.  We’ll do what we can to make that a priority.  Ship wide comms will make everything easier.  I’m going to need to be in engineering where the crystal is.   I’m not exactly sure how to make the Wayfinder work but bringing them together with the Force seems the logical thing.”** 


He looked at Marina and then back to the others.  **”If some of the ideas hold, once the ship is purged of the whispers the ship may begin a repair cycle.”**

Marina shifts slightly, resting a hand on the back of the lounge seating. **"That's the theory Gaxx and I were leaning toward, Wes. The ship's entire architecture is Force-reactive. Purging the Whispers should allow the core to re-establish its original resonance, which might trigger automated maintenance protocols we've never seen before."**

Sera’s eyes widen at the mention of a recursive repair cycle. **"A ship that fixes itself... that's some high-end ancient tech right there. If that happens, we're not just bringing back a derelict; we're bringing back a shipyard in a single vessel."** She taps her chin thoughtfully. **"But if you're in Engineering for the 'tuning' part, we definitely need someone on the Bridge. If the ship starts waking up, someone has to be there to manage the systems—and more importantly, to make sure the computer knows we’re the pilots and not more contamination."**

Echo remains near the ramp, her expression unreadable but her eyes following the discussion. **"If we split again, we can cover both points simultaneously. We know the routes now, and with Sera's new signal booster, we won't be flying blind on the comms."**

Wes nodded as the others spoke.  The information he and Marina just imparted about the possibility of a recursive repair cycle seemed to grab Sera’s attention.   Echo who kept her emotions in check raised the idea he and Marina had already talked about, splitting up.  


Wes nodded at both women and looked at Echo.   He noticed how she was near the ramp.  Almost positioning herself to be the first off or to escape.   He knew her encounter with the custodian and the Force entity was unnerving.  It wasn’t an everyday occurrence to come in contact with a four thousand year old ghost in the Force.   


**”Thats’s the plan.  Two groups.  One in engineering and one on the bridge.  Both stations will need attention when we attempt to purge the ship of the whispers and the first moments right after as things begin to come back online.  I have a feeling it will be chaotic at first.”**  


Taking a couple steps he moved to the lounge seat that Marina was resting her hands on.  With a motion of his hand he offered the seat to her.   Then sat down next to her.   

**”I’m going to need Marina’s help in Engineering.  Other than bringing the Wayfinder in contact with the heart of the Shadow we’re not sure what else needs to be done.   Her knowledge and ability with the Force will be needed as I fly by the seat of my pants.  So to speak.”** 


He looked away from Marina and back to Sera and Echo.   **”I’ll need you two up on the bridge to handle things there as they come back on line.  Before we begin the process we can assess where Roric would best serve which group.  Both locations have importance.”**  He paused for a moment before adding more.  **”Ideas on splitting up the compliment of fixers between both groups.”**  He asked as he looked around.

Sera grins, her crimson skin looking particularly vibrant in the warm light. **"I'm all for the bridge. If that ancient computer starts talking, I want to be the one to answer."** She glances at Echo. **"Between the two of us, we can keep the command deck locked down."**

Marina accepts the seat with a small, grateful nod to Wes, settling in as she adjusts her position to remain comfortable. She looks at Sera and Echo, her expression serious but supportive. **"Wes is right. Engineering will be the focal point for the harmonization, and the Force resonance will be intense.**” She pauses for a moment as she considers. “**The fixers are versatile, but their priority should be where the technical load is greatest. Engineering will likely see the most immediate physical feedback from the reawakening—surge suppressors blowing, ancient conduits finally giving up. I’d recommend taking two with us, and giving one to Team Bridge. Sera can use it for fine-tuning the bridge interfaces while Echo provides the overwatch."**

Roric, who had been listening silently while finishing his rifle check, looks up. **"The bridge is a bottleneck, easier to defend with fewer boots if you have a scout like Echo. Engineering is vast, more angles of approach. I'll stick with Team Engineering. My ion rifle will carry more weight in those open bays."**

Wes nodded as the others spoke.  They had the beginnings of a plan to tackle the mission.   A two pronged approach between Engineering and the Bridge.  While Marina helped him in Engineering under the protective watch of Roric, Sera and Echo would be on the bridge.   Dealing with the reawakening of the ancient capital ship.   


As Roric spoke to where he wished to be, Wes gave the veteran soldier a nod of approval.  **”Good.  Knowing that we will have you there on overwatch will be one less thing we have to worry about.”** He took a few seconds to look around the room at all of them.  


**”While we’re not going in blind this time and have foreknowledge of what to expect don’t let your guard down.  Since the ancient Pathfinder shut down the *Shadow’s* protective droids we *should* be able to traverse unhindered.”**  He made sure to emphasize the word, should.   **”While we were able to leave uneventfully, we're not sure the return trip will be the same.  I have my own suspicions that we won’t encounter any resistance like last time but be prepared.”**  


He looked at the four that were with him and knew that Kael was listening from the cockpit.   **“Any questions, thoughts?”**

A heavy silence follows Wes's words, the weight of the upcoming mission settling over the group. The hum of the *Seventh Moon* is the only sound in the lounge, a steady vibration that feels far more robust than it did only days prior.

Roric gives a sharp, single nod. **"Clear as flimsi, Wes. I'll be in the hold checking the magnetic clamps on the ion gear. Give a shout if the plan changes."** He stands, his heavy boots thudding against the deck as he gathers his tools and heads aft toward the storage lockers.

Echo offers a final, silent nod of agreement. She doesn't speak, her sharp eyes scanning the holographic map one last time as if committing the service corridors to memory. She pushes off from the bulkhead and follows Roric toward the back of the ship, likely to spend the remaining hours in a state of quiet, focused meditation or gear maintenance.

Sera stretches her arms over her head, her crimson skin catching the lounge lights. **"I'm going to run one last diagnostic on the signal booster. If we're going to be talking to each other across ten decks of ancient hull, I want every decibel I can get."** She shoots Wes a quick wink. **"See you in the cockpit for the reversion sequence."** She slides off the lounge seating and disappears into the secondary terminal alcove.

Marina remains seated next to Wes, her hand still resting near his on the table. She leans back slightly, her posture less rigid now that the team has dispersed. She looks at Wes, her blue eyes reflecting a mix of lingering concern and deep trust. **"The team is ready, Wes. They believe in you. *I* believe in you."** 

She shifts slightly, a small wince of discomfort crossing her face as she tries to find a position that doesn't put pressure on her back. **"We have about two hours before Kael brings us out of hyperspace. I should probably try to take my own advice and close my eyes for a bit, but I suspect my mind is going to be too busy running through core-stabilization math."**

Wes nodded as Roric broke the silence in the room.  Wes gave the soldier a nod of acknowledgment as he headed towards the cargo bay.   He looked at Echo as she nodded and looked at the map one last time.   She was quiet and Wes wondered if she was alright.  If the encounter with the Pathfinder, who had used the Force in an attempt to make her do his bidding, had some lingering effect on the scout.  


He watched as she looked their way one last time.  He gave her a nod before she moved away with the silent grace he had come to expect from her.   As Sera spoke about running a diagnostic on the signal booster.  **”Good work with that Sera.   Working comms will make things that much easier.”**  He watched the red skinned Zeltron slicer stand and gather her things.  When she turned he caught the quick wink before she quickly left.    


Letting out a calming breath he leaned back in the seat and looked at Marina.   He watched as she relaxed, her eyes reflecting the emotions he felt from her.  He reached out and took her hand and gave it a firm squeeze.   **”Thank you Knight Cloudspinner.”**  He gave her a sheepish smile as he moved closer.   As she moved closer he saw her wince and felt the discomfort the pregnancy was putting on her.   Her own words echo Sera’s about getting some rest.     


**”Then let’s take an hour right now, right here.   Meditate with me.  Let’s rest and focus on what we’re about to attempt.   Something that hasn’t been done in four millennia.”**  He gave her a smile.   One that showed the confidence he had in her along with the happiness to hear her at his side for this.

Marina’s tired eyes brighten with a spark of amusement at Wes’s formal use of her new title. **"Knight Cloudspinner,"** she repeats softly, a small, genuine smile finally reaching her eyes. **"I suppose I'll have to get used to the sound of that eventually."** 

Marina looks at him, a playful, slightly skeptical arch to her eyebrow. She’d clearly been eyeing the bunk rooms down the hall, the promise of a flat mattress and a few minutes of real rest more tempting than another session of mental discipline. But as she meets his gaze and feels the steady, reassuring pulse of his presence in the Force, her posture softens. 

**"Meditate, Initiate Del-Fin? You're certainly becoming more 'Jedi' than when we met on Fakir,"** she teases, her voice a soft, warm murmur. She shifts, turning her body fully toward him on the lounge seating, the bulk of her robes rustling against the metal. She lets out a slow, grounding breath, her hand tightening around his. **"But you're right. We shouldn't walk into that ship with our minds cluttered by yesterday's fatigue."**

She moves a few cushions, finding a way to sit that supports her and allows her to relax her posture. She closes her eyes, her breathing slowing as she begins the familiar Jedi technique to quiet the mind. She reaches out through their bond, not with words or images, but with a steady, cooling presence

The central lounge of the *Seventh Moon* falls into a profound silence. The distant thrum of the hyperspace drive becomes a rhythmic, background mantra as Wes and Marina sink into a shared meditation. Through the Force, the walls of the ship seem to fade, replaced by the vast, interconnected web of the 'Path' that Wes has begun to glimpse. They drift together in the quiet current, their spirits intertwining, preparing for the monumental resonance that awaits them at the heart of the *Veiled Shadow*.
